transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ve been planning my whole day around avoiding driving over high bridges. If I can take a different route, I do, even if it’s out of the way. And when I can’t avoid it, I get through it, but I’m gripping the wheel the whole time.
Do you ever have episodes where you feel an intense fear or discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes?
Yes. When I see the bridge coming up, it hits pretty quick. My chest tightens, my hands get sweaty on the wheel, and I just stare straight ahead like I’m trying to get myself to the other side.
Do you experience this kind of fear or discomfort in situations other than driving over high bridges?

Not really, no. It’s pretty much those high bridges over the bay. I know they’re built fine and people drive over them every day, but when I get close, my mind goes straight to thinking the car could somehow go over the side.
Do you worry about other situations where you might be in a similar high place, like being on the top floor of a building?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed that being a problem for me. I don’t spend much time on top floors, but it’s not something I worry about the way I do with those bridges.
Is your fear of driving over high bridges the only situation that causes you significant anxiety?

Yeah, as far as I can tell it’s really just those high bridges over the bay. I know they’re safe and people drive them all the time, but when I get close, my mind goes right to the car somehow going over the side.
Do you find yourself worrying about everyday things, like work, finances, or relationships, even when there's no apparent reason to worry?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have normal worries like anyone, but I don’t sit around worrying about work or money or relationships for no reason. That’s not really what’s been bothering me.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things in general, even when there isn't a specific situation like the bridge causing you anxiety?
No, not really. I don’t feel like I’m worrying about everything in general. It’s more when that specific bridge situation comes up.
Do you feel anxious or on edge most of the time, even when you're not thinking about driving over bridges?
No, I wouldn’t say I’m on edge most of the time. When I’m not dealing with that bridge thing, I feel pretty normal.
Do you think you would feel anxious if you were on a high bridge but not driving, for example, if you were walking or riding as a passenger?

Yeah, I think I probably would. I know those big bridges over the bay are built safe and people go over them all day, but when I get near one, my mind just goes to, like, what if the car goes over the side. Even if I wasn’t driving, I think being up there would still make me nervous.
Would your anxiety about the bridge be less if someone else was driving?

Maybe a little, but not a lot. Even if someone else was driving, once we got near the bridge I’d still be thinking, you know, those bridges are probably built fine, people drive them every day... but my mind still jumps to the car going over the side.
Do you feel anxious when you think about the bridge when you're not actually near it or about to cross it?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think it hits me the same way if I’m just sitting somewhere thinking about it. It’s more when I know I’m getting close to one or might have to cross it.
Do you feel anxious about other specific situations or objects, besides high bridges?
Not really, no. I can’t think of anything else specific that gets to me like those high bridges do.
Do you feel like your anxiety about the bridge is part of a broader pattern of worry in your life?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal stuff, but I haven’t noticed it being some bigger pattern. It really seems tied to the high bridges.
Do you think your anxiety would decrease if you were able to completely avoid high bridges for the rest of your life?

Yeah, I think so. If I knew I never had to deal with those high bridges, I probably wouldn’t be worrying about it much. A lot of what’s bothering me is having to plan my day or my route around avoiding them, and if I can’t avoid one, I’m just tense the whole time crossing it.
Would you feel anxious in other situations where you are in a high place but not in control, such as being a passenger in a car on a steep mountain road?
I’m not really sure. I can’t say I’ve noticed that the same way. It’s mostly the bridge thing that stands out to me.
Would you feel anxious if you were a passenger in an airplane?
I’m not sure. I don’t fly much, so I can’t really say I’ve noticed that being a problem. It’s the high bridges that really get to me.
Would your anxiety about being on a high bridge decrease if you were in a situation where you could not fall off, such as being on a completely enclosed bridge?

Maybe a little, if it was totally enclosed. But I think I’d still get nervous just knowing I’m up on a high bridge. I know those bridges over the bay are built fine and people drive them every day, but when I get near one, my mind acts like the car could go right over the side.
Would your anxiety about high bridges be significantly reduced if you were to walk across the bridge, rather than driving?

I don’t think walking would really make it much better. It’s the being up on that high bridge that gets me. I know it’s safe and people go over it all the time, but my mind still goes right to, “what if I could go over the side?”
